title: Composition Versus Inheritance
subtopics: Choosing composition when an inheritance relationship is inappropriate
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of composition versus inheritance and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—object composition—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study composition versus inheritance with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you choose between inheritance, interfaces, and composition based on the relationship being modeled. In this lesson, focus on object composition and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A class defines state and behavior; an object is an instance. Encapsulation protects invariants by keeping mutable state private and validating updates through a small public API. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect object composition with delegating behavior before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Object composition
items.text: A class defines state and behavior; an object is an instance. Encapsulation protects invariants by keeping mutable state private and validating updates through a small public API.

items.title: Delegating behavior
items.text: Use Path and Files for modern file operations, choose byte or character APIs based on the data, and close resources reliably. Parse external files defensively because their contents may be incomplete or malformed.

items.title: Coupling and flexibility
items.text: Inheritance models a substitutable “is-a” relationship, interfaces define contracts, and composition connects collaborators. Polymorphic calls use the runtime object’s override rather than the reference variable’s declared class. Apply that reasoning specifically to coupling and flexibility and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.

items.title: Choosing composition when an inheritance relationship is inappropriate
items.text: Use inheritance for a genuine substitutable relationship, interfaces to express contracts, and composition to combine collaborators. Dynamic dispatch selects an overridden instance method based on the runtime object.
